key_insight: ExpectileGCN learns how to aggregate graph neighborhoods beyond the mean, capturing class-relevant distributional differences, especially in heterophilic graphs.
engineering_relevance: Adaptive aggregation may improve graph-based prediction and resilience to corrupted features or perturbed connections.
method: Learn an expectile level that shifts aggregation between minimum- and maximum-type behavior, with the mean as a special case.
Use sigmoid smoothing and fixed-point iterations for end-to-end differentiation.
Analyze stability, transductive generalization, and classification risk under heterophilic neighborhood models.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong predictive performance and improved robustness on homophilic and heterophilic benchmarks, but provides no dataset names or numerical results.
watch_item: Fixed-point iterations introduce computational and convergence considerations whose practical costs are not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: Graph Representation Learning via Adaptive Expectile Aggregation
